sentences.text: 1 Heard the petition finally with the consent of the parties.

The present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been preferred against the in action on the part of the respondents in not reviewing the order of dismissal from service of the petitioner dated 16.03.2011, in view of his acquittal in Criminal Case No. 1111/2005, wherein the petitioner was tried for an offence under Section 409, 420, 408, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.

Brief facts of the case are that the petitioner was working as an Assistant Grade-III under the respondent department and was posted in SADO Bhitarwar, District Gwalior at the relevant point of time and vide order dated 14.10.1996 he was suspended on his being implicated in a criminal case no.7/1996 in which he was tried vide Session Case No.32/1999 and later on was acquitted vide judgment dated 03.11.2000.

Later on the then officer in-charge of the petitioner since was prejudiced with the petitioner because the petitioner had made some complaints against him for illegal withdrawal from GPF account of petitioner in some other name, and due to enmity the said officer in-charge taking advantage of the family dispute, registration of crime, arrest warrant issued pursuant to that and the suspension order passed earlier, got another false case registered against the petitioner vide Crime No.240/1996 alleging embezzlement of Rs.20,000/- of salary and training expenses of some of the employees.
The petitioner was tried in the aforesaid crime and vide judgment dated 03.11.2000 he was convicted under Section 409 of IPC under the aforesaid crime.
Pursuant to the order of conviction, the petitioner was dismissed from service vide order dated 16.03.2011, without conducting any departmental enquiry.

Thereafter, the present petitioner preferred a Criminal Appeal No.40/2011 against the said conviction which was allowed vide judgment dated 21.09.2011 and the order of conviction was set aside and the petitioner was set free.
Against the said order of acquittal the State had preferred an appeal which was numbered as Criminal Appeal No.1200/2012 before this Court, which is still pending.
After the acquittal, the petitioner moved an application before the respondents and made prayer for his reinstatement in service.

As the said representation was not decided by the respondents, W.P.
no.1526/2012 came to be filed by the present petitioner seeking directions for the respondents therein for considering his representation and reinstating him in service.

The said W.P. was disposed of vide order dated 27.02.2012 directing the petitioner to resubmit his representation and further directing the respondent no.2 to consider the representation and pass reasoned and speaking order and communicate the same to the petitioner.

In pursuance to the directions of this Court the respondents vide Annexure P/1 dated 05.06.2012 rejected the representation of the petitioner on the ground that since a criminal appeal is pending against the acquittal of the petitioner before the High Court, he cannot be reinstated in service.
Aggrieved by the aforesaid order passed by respondents, the present petition has been filed.

Learned counsel for the petitioner while placing reliance in the matter of Ranglal Kushwah vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh and Ors. reported in W.P. No.8183/2019 dated 09.11.2021 submitted that mere pendency of an appeal against the order of acquittal cannot be regarded as continuance of the trial and cannot be treated to be pendency of judicial proceedings as the initial presumption of innocence gets re-enforced by the orders of acquittal.

sentences.text: It was further contended that though the matter cited pertains to a teacher who was illegally and forceably kept out of service by the management of the School but the analogy laid down therein covers the present case, as the petitioner was not reinstated immediately after his acquittal rather the matter was lingered on by the respondents only on the ground that since the criminal appeal was pending before the High Court against the order of acquittal of the petitioner, he is not entitled for reinstatement was per se illegal.
Thus, he prayed that apart from reinstatement, the petitioner be granted full back wages for the period he was kept out of service.

Per contra, Shri Vijay Sundaram, panel lawyer placing reliance in the matter of Vinod Kumar Tomar vs. Union of India and Ors. passed in W.A No.130/2015 dated 09.09.2015 contended that in similar facts, the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court had dismissed the plea of the appellant/petitioner therein and had rejected his claim and, therefore, no illegality can be said to have been committed by the competent authority in rejecting the representation.

sentences.text: On the strength of the above arguments it was submitted that, the present petition has no force and, therefore, it deserved to be dismissed.
Heard the counsels for the parties and perused the record.

The facts of the case revealed and which are admitted by the parties are that a Criminal Case under Sections 409, 420, 408, 467, 468, 471 of IPC was initially registered against the petitioner vide Crime No.240/1996, the learned Trial Court after appreciation of evidence on record held the petitioner to be guilty under Section 409, but acquitted the petitioner for the other offenses.

Against the said order of conviction the present petitioner had preferred an appeal which was allowed vide judgment dated 21.09.2011 and the petitioner was acquitted from the charge under Section 409 also.

Thereafter, the respondent/State had preferred an application for leave to appeal, challenging the acquittal of the petitioner before this Court which was allowed and the case was registered under Criminal Appeal No.561/2014,
which is still pending for final adjudication.
It is an admitted fact that though an appeal has been preferred by the State against the acquittal of the present petitioner, but the effect and operation of the judgment dated 21.09.2011 in Criminal Appeal No.40/2011 preferred by the petitioner had not been stayed, only the appeal preferred by the State is pending and until and unless petitioner is not held guilty in appeal, his innocence will have to be presumed.

The judgment which has been cited by the learned counsel for the petitioner in the matter of Ranglal Kushwah (supra) though pertains to payment of the retiral dues in case when revision against the acquittal of petitioner was pending at the behest of the State, and, the coordinate Bench of this Court has come to a conclusion, while placing reliance in the matter of M.P.

sentences.text: 3 the preferment of a criminal revision or an appeal against the order of acquittal cannot be regarded as continuance of the trial and cannot be treated to be pendency of judicial proceedings as the initial presumption of innocence gets re-enforced by the orders of acquittal and has embarked on a conclusion, and had directed the respondents to release the retiral dues of the petitioner.
This Court is in full agreement with the analogy which has been laid down by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in the matter o f Ranglal Kushwah (supra).

It is true that pendency of a criminal appeal against the order of acquittal cannot be said to be a continuation of the trial and cannot be treated to be the pendency of judicial proceedings and the order of acquittal pre supposes innocence of the person and a person would be treated innocent until he is proved guilty.

In the present case the admitted position which has not been controverted or denied by the learned panel lawyer for the State is that the petitioner has been acquitted of the charges under Section 409 by the appellate Court.
The order of acquittal is still in existence, the effect and operation of it has not been stayed by this Court in the criminal appeal which is pending at the behest of the State.

Thus, in the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, the rejection of the petitioner's representation which is solely on the ground of pendency of appeal alone cannot be sustained and is hereby quashed.
The respondents are directed to reinstate the petitioner forthwith.
So far as claim of the petitioner with regard to payment of salary for the period he was kept out of service alleging it to be illegal on the part of the respondents is concerned

, the analogy which has been laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Deepali Gundu Surwase vs. Kranti Junior Adhyapak Mahavidyalaya (D.Ed.) and Ors. (supra) can very well be applied in the present case also.

entities.text: Deepali Gundu Surwase vs. Kranti Junior Adhyapak Mahavidyalaya (D.Ed.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner who was acquitted by a competent Court was required to be reinstated as the order of termination was solely based upon his conviction in the criminal case and there was no separate departmental enquiry conducted.

Since as the petitioner brought to the knowledge of the respondents that he has been acquitted of the charges framed against him in the criminal case, the respondents should have reinstated the petitioner forthwith.

Though the respondents were right in their power to have further agitate the order of acquittal before higher forum, but admittedly as this Court has already held above that mere filing of an appeal or pendency of an appeal would not amount to continuance of the trial or cannot be treated to be pendency of judicial proceedings as the initial presumption of innocence gets re-enforced by the orders of acquittal and also since the effect and operation of the order of acquittal was not stayed, the petitioner is right in saying that he was illegally kept out of service and it can very well be said that denial of back wages to any employee would amount to indirectly punishing the concerned employee and rewarding the employer by relieving him of the obligation to pay back wages including the emoluments.

The Hon'ble Apex Court has also in the case of Deepali Gundu Surwase vs. Kranti Junior Adhyapak Mahavidyalaya (D.Ed.) and Ors. (supra) has held that the cases in which the competent Court or Tribunal finds that the employer has acted in gross violation of the statutory provisions and/or the principles of natural justice or is guilty of victimizing the employee or workman, then the concerned Court or Tribunal will be fully justified in directing payment of full back wages from date he had submitted his representation for his reinstatement.
